problem: Subcontractor invoices came in by mail and email to six project managers, and approvals sat on desks for weeks. Subs called the office every Friday asking when they would be paid.
approach: Moved every invoice into one queue, matched each one to its purchase order, and sent approvals to project managers on their phones at the job site.
result_metric: Days to approve a subcontractor invoice
quote: Our PMs approve invoices from the job site now. Nobody chases paper on Friday afternoons anymore.

problem: Invoices could not be paid until a signed lien waiver came back, and the waivers lived in a shared inbox. Payments ran late and vendors put jobs on hold.
approach: Tied each lien waiver to its invoice, held payment until the waiver arrived, and sent the vendor a reminder when one was missing.
quote: We stopped getting calls from suppliers threatening to pull crews. That alone was worth it.

industry: transportation, logistics, supply chain and storage
problem: Thousands of carrier invoices arrived every month, and the team paid them too late to get the early payment discounts carriers offered.
approach: Matched carrier invoices against load records automatically and scheduled each payment inside its discount window.
quote: We were leaving discount money on the table every week. Now the system pays on day nine by default.

industry: transportation, logistics, supply chain and storage
problem: Fuel, repair and toll invoices for a fleet of 90 trucks were keyed in by two people, and closing the month took nine working days.
approach: Read fuel and repair invoices automatically, coded each one to the right truck, and sent only the exceptions to a person.
result_metric: Working days to close the month
quote: Close used to eat the first two weeks of every month. Now it is done before the first Friday.

problem: Supply invoices for 14 clinics were keyed in by hand at the central office, and every clinic manager approved them by email.
approach: Collected invoices from every clinic in one place, routed approvals by location, and matched supply orders to what was received.
result_metric: Working days to close the month
quote: Clinic managers approve in a minute instead of digging through email. Our close takes less than half the time it did.

problem: Twenty-two offices ordered their own supplies, and the two-person AP team spent most of the week matching packing slips to invoices.
approach: Each office took a photo of the packing slip on delivery, and invoices were matched against it automatically.
result_metric: Hours a week spent on AP
quote: My team gets to do finance work again instead of matching paper.

problem: Software bills were spread across 40 company cards, and finance only heard about renewals after they were charged.
approach: Pulled every vendor bill into one list with an owner and a renewal date, and flagged each renewal 30 days ahead.
quote: We found three tools nobody had opened since spring.

problem: The founder still approved every bill by hand, and payments waited whenever she was traveling.
approach: Set approval rules by amount and vendor, so routine bills paid on schedule and only new vendors or large amounts went to the founder.
result_metric: Founder hours on bills each month
quote: I approve maybe five bills a month now, and they are the ones I should be looking at.

problem: Raw material invoices were matched to purchase orders and receipts in spreadsheets, and supplier price changes slipped through.
approach: Ran a three-way match on every invoice and flagged any line where the price differed from the purchase order.
result_metric: Invoices handled per AP clerk each month
quote: We caught a supplier billing the old steel price for three months straight. The first week paid for the year.

problem: Ingredient suppliers sent invoices by email, by mail and through portals, and the same invoice sometimes got paid twice.
approach: Collected invoices from every channel in one place and checked each new invoice against everything already paid.
quote: Every duplicate we paid was money we had to chase back. Now they never go out.

problem: Contractor and vendor invoices piled up across nine branch offices, and late fees showed up on almost every statement.
approach: Routed invoices from every branch to one approver and scheduled payments by due date instead of by when someone got to them.
quote: Late fees were a line item we had stopped questioning. Now they are close to zero.

problem: Maintenance vendors sent invoices for 60 buildings to property managers, who forwarded them to accounting when they had time.
approach: Gave every building its own invoice inbox, coded invoices to the property automatically, and sent approvals to the right manager.
result_metric: Days to approve a maintenance invoice
quote: Our plumbers and electricians get paid on time, so they pick up when we call.
